rule: Domain assessment only. No combined war score and no arithmetic aggregation across casualties, commanders, money, equipment, territory, or munitions.

contrary_evidence: Iran retained strike capability and later regional attacks continued.
domains.assessment: U.S./coalition retained the ability to generate sustained long-range strikes. Continued Iranian attacks show strike superiority did not equal opponent paralysis.

contrary_evidence: US-ALUDEID CAOC was rendered inoperable; Iran achieved precise damage at several regional sites.
domains.assessment: Distributed U.S. C2 architecture preserved campaign command despite loss of a major forward node. Iran still demonstrated useful target-quality data and precision at some fixed sites.

supporting_evidence: High reported interception rates in current atlas/CSIS baseline.
contrary_evidence: Verified base damage, THAAD/Patriot equipment damage, U.S. casualties, and depleted interceptor inventories.
domains.assessment: Defenses prevented much larger damage but were not impermeable and incurred meaningful inventory/equipment costs.

U.S. naval forces retained interdiction/strike capacity. Iran retained enough coercive leverage, risk generation and routing influence to suppress normal commercial Hormuz traffic. Neither maps cleanly to absolute 'control'.

contrary_evidence: Later lower launch tempo, but July/August attacks and threats continued.
domains.assessment: Iran expended very large opening inventories and suffered substantial attrition pressure, yet retained enough launch capacity for continued coercive and lethal effects.

contrary_evidence: U.S. carrier deployments extended/rotated; Iranian durable loss ledger remains incomplete.
Iran retained missile/UAS launch capacity, IRGC small craft, coercive Hormuz leverage and the ability to impose lethal/local effects on U.S. and partner forces.
domains.assessment: The public record now supports a comparative force-preservation judgment: Iran's conventional force absorbed substantially deeper durable attrition while U.S./coalition campaign-generating capacity remained broadly intact. This is not a claim that Iran was disarmed or strategically incapable; surviving missile/UAS, small-craft and Hormuz coercive capabilities remained consequential.

contrary_evidence: Some allies declined Hormuz escort participation; mediators continued engagement with Iran.
domains.assessment: Iranian pressure did not consistently fracture regional alignment and at times drove closer security/economic coordination, though partner willingness to join specific military missions varied.

contrary_evidence: Chinese crude purchases and alternative trade channels showed continuity; GCC growth forecasts were also heavily damaged by Hormuz disruption.
domains.assessment: Iran faced severe inflation, export and FX pressure, but broader Gulf/global economic damage was also substantial. Do not reduce this to a single side score.
